submission.hypothesis: The exact current Runtime-owned causal boundary is the pair of gates hard-coded on the Core admission path `admit_new_task_with_inputs` (engine.rs), not in MCP or the dispatcher. First, run_task_proposal_with_inputs validates the proposal, canonicalizes input bindings, computes the `runtime-request-input-v2:` identity, and (on new admission) resolves the proposal and re-validates structure before `admit_new_task_with_inputs`. That function refuses `execution_target == WindowsNative` ("windows_native immutable input bindings are not implemented in R-W2", line 501-506) and refuses any profile other than `ContainedLocal` (line 507-511). Because `bind_bound` in the MCP adapter structurally forces `execution_profile: ContainedLocal` (mod.rs bind_bound, line 526) and the request identity for input-bound proposals is keyed only by proposal+inputs, the practical admission block is the WindowsNative early-return inside `admit_new_task_with_inputs`. This is distinct from (and upstream of) the separate, policy-independent `validate_run_request_structure` check at engine.rs:4914-4926 which rejects non-trusted_local profiles for windows_native (the "windows_native currently supports trusted_local only" message), and from `current_execution_provider_snapshot` engine.rs:1356-1372 which requires explicit Windows provider config. The dispatch path is also asymmetric: `dispatch_attempt` (engine.rs:2292-2347) materializes/re-verifies `input_set_path` only in the LocalLinux arm; the WindowsNative arm (windows_systemd_run, windows.rs:343) takes no input-set argument and the launcher command has no input-set passthrough. So the frozen owner line that blocks exact immutable-input windows_native admission is engine.rs:501-506 (plus the profile gate at 507-511 that the MCP adapter already satisfies), and the physical dispatch gap is the missing input-set handoff in the WindowsNative dispatch arm that nothing in this revision implements.
submission.causalMechanism: workspace.execBound MCP tool -> bind_bound forces ExecutionProfile::ContainedLocal and carries caller-supplied input bindings (authority name, relative object, expected SHA-256, presentation-relative path) -> run_task_proposal_with_inputs (engine.rs:464) canonicalizes bindings, computes the input-bound proposal identity (runtime-request-input-v2:), idempotent-registry lookup, then on new admission calls admit_new_task_with_inputs. That function's first gate rejects execution_target==WindowsNative unconditionally (engine.rs:501-506, "windows_native immutable input bindings are not implemented in R-W2"), and its second gate requires ContainameedLocal profile (engine.rs:507-511). Neither gate lives in Authority/World/Agent argument space: authority roots are operator-owned `input_authorities` opened at Runtime construction (engine.rs:338-375), and the proposal profile/value cannot be overridden by caller since bind_bound hard-code-containers it. The dispatch side is asymmetric: only the LocalLinux arm of dispatch_attempt (engine.rs:2293-2318) re-verifies frozen effective inputs via verify_effective_input_set and passes input_set_path into systemd_run; the WindowsNative arm (engine.rs:2320-2347 -> windows_systemd_run) has no input-set parameter, no launcher flag, and no re-verification. The plan struct (RuntimeExecutionPlan, types.rs:622-663) already carries input_set_id/effective_inputs uniformly, so the data model and identity are target-agnostic; the block is purely the two hard-coded admission gates in admit_new_task_with_inputs plus the absent Windows dispatch handoff.

Even stronger: directly call admit_new_task_with_inputs (or reconcile the LocalLinux-arm-only input_set_path at engine.rs:2293-2318) with a windows_native plan whose effective_inputs are non-empty to confirm there is no code path in dispatch_attempt that transfers Job-owned input bytes to the Windows launcher, establishing that admission and dispatch are each independently Windows-unaware for immutable inputs and that both must change, not just the MCP tool or World/Agent args.
